To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-10 production is induced by high TCR signaling in Th1 cells and requires IL-12-induced activation of STAT4 transcription factor and ERK MAP kinases.
IL-10 expression by Th1 cells requires IL-12-induced Stat4 activation, ERK1 and 2 activation, and c-maf expression, and that IL-10 production is induced by repeated TCR triggering.
IL-10 production is induced in Th1 cells by high T cell receptor ligation and IL-12 signaling, and that IL-10 expression correlates with c-maf induction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the signals that regulate IL-10-producing CD4+ Th1 cells.
the development of IL10-producing Th1 cell subsets and the signaling pathways required for their development.
the signals required for the development of IL10-producing Th1, Th17, and Th2 cells, and the mechanisms that control IL-10 production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the production of IL- 10 is a common feature of all Th cells, which requires high antigen dose and ERK1 and 2 activation.

IL-10 production in Th cells requires high-dose T-cell antigen receptor ligation, IL-12-induced activation of the STAT4 transcription factor, and sustained activation of the ERK1 and 2 mitogen-activated protein kinases.
Th cell subsets require distinct transcription factors for their development, but share ERK1 and 2 activation and IL-10 production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-10-producing CD4 T cells can be induced by high antigen dose in the presence of IL-12, and that ERK MAP kinases and STAT4 are required to direct this response.
IL-10 production in Th1, Th17, and Th2 cells is controlled by the activation of distinct signal transduction pathways and STAT factors.
the development of IL10-producing Th cells requires high-dose T cell receptor ligation and the activation of STAT4 and ERK MAP kinases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development and maintenance IL-10-producing cells require sustained activation of ERK and STAT4.
IL-10 production is not a default pathway for Th cells, but rather requires a specific set of stimuli.

IL-10 production is an integral part of Th1 differentiation and that IL-10 expression by Th1 cells is regulated by high-dose T cell receptor ligation, ERK1 and 2 activation, and IL-10-induced STAT4 activation.
